name: tumblr-mcp
description: Tumblr (social): me, analytics_post. Every tool maps to a documented endpoint.

platform_mcp_tumblr_api_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_TUMBLR_API_KEY
platform_mcp_tumblr_api_key.description: The OAuth Consumer Key of an app registered at https://www.tumblr.com/oauth/apps, sent as the `api_key` query parameter ('API key: Requires an API key. Use your OAuth Consumer Key as your api_key', https://www.tumblr.com/docs/en/api/v2#authentication). It only unlocks the public blog methods; everything at the 'OAuth' level (posting, notes, user info, deletion) needs a signed OAuth 1.0a request or an OAuth2 user token and is listed under not_offered.

platform_mcp_tumblr_blog_identifier.title: PLATFORM_MCP_TUMBLR_BLOG_IDENTIFIER
platform_mcp_tumblr_blog_identifier.description: The blog to read, as its blog name (staff), hostname (staff.tumblr.com or a custom domain) or UUID (t:0aY0xL2Fi1OFJg4YxpmegQ) ('blog-identifier', https://www.tumblr.com/docs/en/api/v2#blog-identifiers); env PLATFORM_MCP_TUMBLR_BLOG_IDENTIFIER.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /v2/blog/{blog-identifier}/info?api_key= (API key level) returns {meta{status, msg}, response{blog{title, posts, name, updated, description, ask, ask_anon, likes, url, uuid, avatar[], ...}}}; the 'account' is the configured blog (account.response.blog), and a rejected consumer key is a 401 auth_error. The API-key level cannot say which user owns the key (/v2/user/info is OAuth-level, https://www.tumblr.com/docs/en/api/v2#userinfo--get-a-users-information).

tools.name: analytics_post
tools.description: GET /v2/blog/{blog-identifier}/posts?api_key=&id=<post id> (API key level; `id`: 'A specific post ID. Returns the single post specified or (if not found) a 404 error') returns {meta, response{blog, posts[{id, id_string, post_url, type, timestamp, date, note_count, tags, ...}], total_posts}}; the counts come from response.posts[0]. Tumblr's only public metric is `note_count` (likes + reblogs + replies combined); the runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so it is a top-level field. Only published posts of the configured blog are visible.
